sources.title: Meinolf Geck, Modular Representations of Hecke Algebras, EPFL course notes (arXiv:math/0511548v2)
sources.locator: Complete 54-page PDF; inspected §2, printed/PDF pp. 6–7, and §4.1 with Theorems 4.2–4.4, printed/PDF pp. 15–16, for the exact Hecke normalization, trace context, generic semisimplicity hypotheses and split-label cautions.

contents.name: Section 2, finite Hecke basis and canonical symmetrizing trace convention
contents.reason: The rank-one counterexample defines the delta-at-identity functional itself and computes its form locally; no missing HH-13 proof is imported.

contents.name: Section 4.1 and Theorem 4.2, generic finite-Coxeter Hecke semisimplicity
contents.reason: The notes establish the finite-Hecke deformation conclusion under their stated split hypotheses; the item instead proves its exact non-split-safe regular-trace sufficient condition directly.

contents.name: Theorem 4.3, Tits correspondence for irreducible characters
contents.reason: The local theorem only identifies labels in an explicitly split formal deformation and does not assert generic splitness or a character correspondence for arbitrary finite Hecke specializations.

contents.name: Theorem 4.4, Schur elements and cyclotomic factors
contents.reason: This batch proves a regular-trace determinant certificate and its rank-one boundary only; Schur-element formulas and their modular divisibility consequences are not needed.

sources.title: Maarten Solleveld, Affine Hecke Algebras and Their Representations, author-hosted survey
sources.locator: Complete 80-page PDF; inspected §1.1, PDF pp. 4–5, including normalized finite Hecke relations, the symmetric trace, Theorem 1.1 and its rank-one example.

contents.name: Section 1.1, normalized finite-Hecke relations and symmetric trace
contents.reason: The Laurent parameter convention is matched to the locally defined standard basis; the regular trace is separately defined by traces of left multiplication.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1, polynomial semisimplicity locus for finite-dimensional deformations
contents.reason: The local theorem retains only the determinant-nonvanishing implication and proves it from the group-algebra fiber, without importing the stronger split conclusion.

contents.name: Lemma 1.7 and later affine-Hecke radical results
contents.reason: The batch is restricted to finite Coxeter groups and finite-dimensional Hecke fibers; affine-Hecke radical and Bernstein-presentation results are outside that scope.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof, Structure of Finite Dimensional Algebras, MIT OpenCourseWare 18.712, Chapter 7
sources.locator: Complete 4-page PDF inspected: §7.1, Theorem 7.1; §7.2, Proposition 7.3 and Corollary 7.5; §7.3, Theorem 7.6. The local proof extends the nilpotent-ideal idempotent lift to the complete k[[h]] setting by Newton iteration.

contents.name: Proposition 7.3 and Corollary 7.5, idempotent lifting and complete orthogonal families modulo nilpotent ideals
contents.reason: The source confirms the orthogonal-corner induction; the item proves the complete power-series case with a convergent explicit Newton correction, rather than assuming the ideal is nilpotent.

contents.name: Theorem 7.1 and Definition 7.2, projectives as direct summands of free modules
contents.reason: The item proves the exact finite formal-series special case directly by a finite-generator matrix inverse and h-adic divisibility, without using an unproved projective-module classification.

contents.name: Theorem 7.6, projective covers and matrix-block labels for simple modules
contents.reason: The theorem is for finite-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field; the local formal theorem instead constructs matrix units over k[[h]] and proves its fiber labels directly.

sources.title: Arun Ram, Lectures in Representation Theory, Lecture 5
sources.locator: Complete Lecture 5 page inspected, lines 11–40: Theorem 1.41 states the finite-dimensional regular-trace criterion; Proposition 1.45 gives the Gram-matrix criterion. The page's proof of Theorem 1.41 stops at line 49 with 'Continued next lecture', so only the statement and Gram calculation are corroboration; the item contains the full proof.

contents.name: Theorem 1.41, nondegenerate regular trace and semisimplicity for finite-dimensional algebras
contents.reason: The displayed theorem statement corroborates the implication, but its proof is unfinished on this page; the batch item independently proves radical nilpotence, finite maximal-ideal reduction, and the trace step.

contents.name: Proposition 1.45, a trace is nondegenerate exactly when its Gram matrix is invertible
contents.reason: The item defines the Gram determinant in the explicit standard basis and proves basis-change invariance directly; no unfinished source argument is relied on.

contents.name: §2, Definitions 2.1–2.2: coefficient model and Cauchy product
contents.reason: The item uses this formal coefficient model and convolution but derives the residue map, h-adic completeness, separatedness, and fraction-field claims in its complete local proof.

alternatives.argument: No Wilf result is imported. The item defines the constant-coefficient map, proves its kernel is hR, proves the domain property by least nonzero degree, constructs h-adic limits by eventual coefficients, proves separatedness by coefficient vanishing, and obtains the fraction field from the domain construction. These steps use the published formal-series coefficient definition and ring theorem, the field definition, the integral-domain definition, and the fraction-field theorem.
